text:
julia_recruiter: quick Q — onboarding note: Maria K is converting from contractor -> full-time starting 2026-07-01. She asked whether her 401k eligibility and employer match start immediately or if there's a waiting period. Also curious about vesting of the employer match for prior equity/tenure-based vesting rules.

sam_hr: hi @julia_recruiter :wave: welcome Maria! Two separate things: 1) 401k eligibility: our plan has a first-of-month rule and a 30-day service requirement for employer match eligibility for new W-2 hires. since her start is 2026-07-01, she'll be eligible to enroll for the first payroll after 2026-07-30 (assuming payroll counts days worked).

sam_hr: 2) employer match: match begins on eligible payrolls after enrollment and payroll deductions. we don’t retroactively match for periods when she was classified as a contractor (no payroll deferrals during that time).

alex_finance: adding payroll nuance — there9s a payroll preview cycle. If Maria enrolls in the new hire window and sets deferral before the payroll cutoff (two business days before the pay run) her deferrals can start on the first eligible paycheck. Match will apply on those paychecks.

julia_recruiter: got it. Thanks. What about vesting? She9s been contracting for 18 months prior — does that service count toward the company match vesting schedule?

sam_hr: good question. Contractor service does not count as credited service for 401k match vesting under the plan document. Vesting uses service as an employee (W-2) only. However, if there are special circumstances (like a contract-to-hire agreement that explicitly credits prior service), we can check written offer terms. Do we have that in her offer package?

julia_recruiter: offer says "conversion subject to standard benefits eligibility" — no explicit credit for contractor time. So assume no credit.

alex_finance: finance note: vesting schedule is 3-year graded (33% year1, 67% year2, 100% year3) for match contributions. If Maria starts 7/1, her vesting clock begins on her hire date. Employer contributions made after hire will vest per that schedule.

contractor-bot: FYI: contractors are not eligible for employer-sponsored retirement plan contributions. Please reclassify if you intend to credit prior service.

julia_recruiter: ok. Another tiny thing — can she roll any retirement savings from a solo 401k she had as a contractor into our plan once eligible?

sam_hr: most plans allow incoming rollovers from qualified plans, but it depends on the trustee/vendor acceptance. We'll need: rollover paperwork, plan account statements, and trustee-to-trustee instructions. Recommend she waits until she9s fully enrolled and then initiates with our vendor.

alex_finance: reach out to transfers@forus.example when ready. Forus typically accepts rollovers and will provide the incoming rollover form. Also note there9s an option to do a direct trustee transfer to avoid withholding.

benefits-bot: Helpful link: https://benefits.redwood.example/new-hires-401k (see "Eligibility, Vesting & Rollovers")

julia_recruiter: perfect — I'll tell Maria: enroll as soon as she9s eligible, plan for match starting after first eligible paycheck, contractor time likely doesn't count toward vesting unless documented, and she can roll in solo 401k later. Thanks everyone! :tada:
